Ordination Wrapper Function

Source: R/ordination.r
ordination.Rd

Runs any of ecodive's ordination methods by name, as beta_div() does for beta diversity metrics.

Usage

ordination(x, method, ...)

Arguments

x

The data to ordinate: for "pcoa" and "nmds", a dist object such as from beta_div(), or a symmetric matrix of distances. See list_ordinations() for what each method takes.

method

The name of an ordination method: "nmds" or "pcoa". Flexible matching is supported (see below). Programmatic access via list_ordinations().

...

Further arguments for the method's function, such as k or cpus. Each method keeps its own defaults; see pcoa() and nmds().

Value

The method's result, as described in "Ordination result" below. ordination(x, 'pcoa', ...) is the same as pcoa(x, ...).

Details

List of Ordination Methods

Option / Function NameMethod Name
nmdsNon-metric Multidimensional Scaling (NMDS)
pcoaPrincipal Coordinates Analysis (PCoA)

Flexible name matching

Case insensitive and partial matching, ignoring anything but letters. E.g. method = 'PCoA' or 'principal coord' selects pcoa. Common other names also work: 'MDS', 'PCO', 'cmdscale', or 'classical MDS' for pcoa, and 'non-metric MDS', 'metaMDS', or 'monoMDS' for nmds.

Finished code should always use the full primary option name to avoid ambiguity with future additions to the list of methods.

Ordination result

Every ordination method (pcoa(), nmds(), and ordination()) returns the same kind of object: a plain numeric matrix with one row per sample (named after the samples) and one column per axis (named "PCoA1", "NMDS1", etc.), so that it can go straight into plot() or a data frame. Its attributes always begin with these three, in this order:

  • method: The method's ID, e.g. "pcoa" or "nmds".

  • eig: Each axis's eigenvalue, or NA for methods without them.

  • prop: The proportion of the total variance that each axis explains, or NA where that isn't defined.

Attributes particular to the method follow them.

See also

pcoa(), nmds(), list_ordinations()

Examples

    d <- bray(ex_counts)

    ordination(d, 'pcoa')
#>             PCoA1       PCoA2        PCoA3
#> Saliva -0.3891250 -0.03721713  0.296748867
#> Gums   -0.3951099 -0.05550727 -0.293514268
#> Nose    0.3179676  0.53707433 -0.006811864
#> Stool   0.4662673 -0.44434993  0.003577264
#> attr(,"method")
#> [1] "pcoa"
#> attr(,"eig")
#> [1] 0.6260388 0.4903619 0.1742697
#> attr(,"prop")
#> [1] 0.4850493 0.3799280 0.1350226
#> attr(,"trace")
#> [1] 1.29067

    ordination(d, 'NMDS', k = 2)
#> Warning: stress is (nearly) zero: there may be too few samples
#>             NMDS1       NMDS2
#> Saliva -0.3891463 -0.03721917
#> Gums   -0.3951316 -0.05551031
#> Nose    0.3179851  0.53710375
#> Stool   0.4662929 -0.44437427
#> attr(,"method")
#> [1] "nmds"
#> attr(,"eig")
#> [1] NA NA
#> attr(,"prop")
#> [1] NA NA
#> attr(,"stress")
#> [1] 0
#> attr(,"converged")
#> [1] FALSE
#> attr(,"tries")
#> [1] 20
#> attr(,"best_try")
#> [1] 0
